No teaching moment

From a post straight to a big decision

Today the step after a post is a free guide or a discovery call for 1:1. For someone who still feels guilty saying no, that's a big leap, so most of them never take it.

No filter

Applicants arrive at very different stages

People book a call after one post that hit home, so your calls mix people ready to start with people who aren't there yet. A class gives every applicant the same foundation first.

No list engine

Growth depends on today's post

With nothing capturing buyers and emails every day, new clients only appear when a post lands, and quiet weeks show up in your calendar.

The followers who love your content but aren't ready for 1:1 today have no paid next step, so most of them take none.

Sound familiar?

Being nice was never the problem. Disappearing to keep the peace is.

  • You're the one everyone leans on, and you're ready to stop saying yes when you mean no.
  • You rehearse a hard conversation for days, then cave in the first thirty seconds.
  • Holding a boundary with someone difficult leaves you second-guessing yourself for a week.
  • You understand the patterns, but knowing hasn't changed what you do in the moment.

Here's what you'll learn

Five things we'll cover in 60 minutes

01

Why "nice" keeps you stuck

Where the urge to please comes from, and why trying harder to keep everyone happy rarely works.

02

Spotting the push-back

The guilt-trips, blame-shifting and silent treatment that make boundaries feel impossible, and how to recognise them as they happen.

03

Boundary words that hold

A simple way to say what you will and won't do, calmly, without over-explaining or apologising.

04

The guilt afterwards

What to do in the hours after you hold a boundary, when the urge to take it back is strongest.

05

Your next step

How the scripts kit and 1:1 coaching work, so you can choose the support that fits you.

Static 3 · Contrast layout · Hook: the nice way vs the No More Nice way

Script 1 · Reel · 30 to 45 seconds

"Nice isn't the same as kind"

Hook
"Being nice and being kind are not the same thing, and mixing them up is costing a lot of people their peace." (to camera, close framing)
Body
"Nice is saying yes so nobody's upset with you. Kind is being honest, including with yourself. Most people pleasers don't need to become harder. They need a few clear words, and a plan for the guilt that shows up afterwards." (text on screen: nice vs kind)
CTA
"I teach the whole thing in a 60-minute class called No More Nice. It's $17 and there's a replay. Tap Sign up to get your seat."
Script 2 · Reel · 30 seconds

"Say this instead"

Hook
"Here's one sentence to use the next time someone asks for something you don't have room for." (Breanne holds up one finger)
Body
"Instead of 'I'm so sorry, I just can't because...' and a long list of reasons, try: 'That doesn't work for me this time.' Then stop talking. The pause will feel huge. Let it." (captions: before / after)
CTA
"That's one script. In No More Nice I'll walk you through how to hold it when someone pushes back. Link below."
Script 3 · Reel · 45 seconds

"Three signs of push-back"

Hook
"When you start setting boundaries, some people push back. Here are three ways it often shows up." (walking, natural light)
Body
"One: guilt. 'After everything I've done for you.' Two: blame. Suddenly the boundary is the problem, not the request. Three: silence, until you give in. Recognising them in the moment makes them much easier to stay steady through."
CTA
"I break down all of it, and what to say back, in my $17 class No More Nice. Tap Sign up."
